privacy.titolo: Notice on the processing of personal data
privacy.chiP: The "Datahue" app is run by its administrator, the person who invited you, who is the data controller. Access is by invitation only. For any request about your data you can write to them at the address you received the invitation from.
privacy.quali1: Email address and, if you sign in with Google, the name and profile picture provided by Google.
privacy.quali2: The files you upload and the tables created from them. They may contain health data (for example blood pressure and heart rate), which the GDPR treats as a special category of data (Art. 9).
privacy.quali3: The charts you save and the technical choices needed for the app to work (sign-in session).
privacy.perchéH: Why and on what legal basis
privacy.perchéP: Only to show you statistics and charts about your data. Health data is processed only with your explicit consent (Art. 9(2)(a) GDPR), which you give at your first sign-in and can withdraw at any time by deleting your account.
privacy.chiVede1: Only you: each user sees only their own data, and the administrator cannot access it from the app either.
privacy.chiVede2: The data is stored with technical providers acting as data processors: Supabase (database and files, servers in Stockholm, EU) and Vercel (running the app, functions in Stockholm, EU).
privacy.chiVede3: There is no advertising, no traffic analytics and no sharing with third parties.
privacy.quantoP: Tables and charts: for as long as you keep your account. The original file you upload is deleted automatically after 30 days (the tables created from it stay). Deleting a dataset removes its table and the original file; deleting your account removes all your data.
privacy.cookieP: The app only uses technical cookies, needed for it to work or chosen by you, so your consent is not required and we only show an information notice. There are no profiling, advertising or traffic-analysis cookies.
privacy.cookie1: Sign-in cookies (the name starts with “sb-”): they keep your session after login and are removed when you sign out.
privacy.cookie2: Language cookie (“lingua”): remembers whether you chose Italian or English and lasts one year.
privacy.cookie3: If you sign in with Google, Google may set its own cookies on its sign-in page, under its own policy.
privacy.dirittiP: You can download your data as CSV or Excel and delete your account with all its data from the <account>My account</account> page. You also have the rights of access, rectification, restriction and objection, and you can lodge a complaint with the Italian data protection authority, the Garante (www.garanteprivacy.it), or with the authority of your country.
privacy.medicoP: The app only shows the data you upload and gives no diagnoses or medical advice. The thresholds in the charts are chosen by you.

benvenuto.titoloAnimazione: From files of numbers to charts
benvenuto.intro: Do you have a spreadsheet with your warehouse orders, this month's expenses or anything else? Upload it and the app turns it into statistics and charts.
benvenuto.soloInvito: Access is by invitation only. If you want to try it, ask for an invitation from whoever sent you the link.
benvenuto.passo1: Drag a CSV or Excel file. You see a preview and choose what to import.
benvenuto.passo2: Averages, minimums and maximums, how often each value appears, trend over time.
benvenuto.passo3: Pick the period or the values you care about: numbers and charts update together.
benvenuto.esempiNota: The data below is made up and only serves to show the charts.
benvenuto.esPressione: A file with date, systolic and diastolic becomes a trend. You can set a threshold: values above it turn red.
benvenuto.esPressioneD: Example: trend of systolic and diastolic pressure over 14 days, with a dashed threshold at 140.
benvenuto.esOrdini: From a list of orders you immediately see which categories weigh the most.
benvenuto.esOrdiniD: Example: 37 orders split by category. Books is the largest.
benvenuto.esSpesa: Sums, averages and counts per period, with the values written above the bars.
benvenuto.esSpesaD: Example: monthly spending from May to October, the highest in September.
benvenuto.cosa1: Upload CSV and Excel files: the app recognises numbers, dates and text by itself.
benvenuto.cosa2: Filter by period, by values or by time of day.
benvenuto.cosa3: Build your own charts (bars, lines, pie and more), save them and pin your favourites to your dashboard.
benvenuto.cosa4: Download charts as images and filtered data as CSV or Excel.
benvenuto.privacy: You only see your own files: no other user can read them. The data is stored in Europe and you can download it or delete everything whenever you want from your account page. The app shows numbers and gives no medical advice.

guidaPagina.intro: Datahue turns a file of numbers into statistics and charts. You use it in seven steps.
guidaPagina.p1Testo: From the “Import” menu drag a CSV or Excel file (up to 50 MB). If the file has several sheets, choose which to import. The app detects encoding and separator on its own; if you see odd characters, change them by hand. Before importing it guides you in four steps: table name, columns and types (number, date, text…), values to check and summary. Values that don't fit the chosen type are marked in red with their row number: you can correct them, leave them empty or skip those rows. Each file (or sheet) becomes a dataset with its own name.
guidaPagina.p2Testo: “My datasets” lists the files you imported, with a search by name. Open one: the “Data” tab shows the table, page by page. From there you can also rename it, download it as CSV or Excel (.xlsx, with numbers and dates ready for calculations) or delete it: to delete it you type DELETE, so it never happens by mistake.
guidaPagina.p3Testo: Above the data, choose a period (also with shortcuts such as “last 7 days” or “last 30 days”), the categories or values you care about, or search for some text. Statistics and charts always follow the chosen filters; “Clear filters” removes them all.
guidaPagina.p4Testo: The “Statistics” tab summarises the file: number of rows, period, averages, trend over time, a summary of each column, a comparison between groups (for example the average by time of day) and the columns that move together. In “Column by column” you can drag the cards into the order you like (the app remembers it; “Reset order” goes back to the file's order) and open one larger with the magnifying glass.
guidaPagina.p5Testo: In the “Charts” tab, choose the type (bars, lines, pie, scatter, histogram, box plot…), the columns and the calculation. The chart updates with every choice. “Save chart” keeps it for next time, among the dataset's “Saved charts”; you can download it as an image (PNG) or as data (CSV).
guidaPagina.p6Testo: Under a saved chart, press “Pin to dashboard”: you'll find it in the “Dashboard” menu, together with the charts pinned from your other datasets. There you can drag them into the order you prefer (also from the keyboard, with the arrows on the handle), open one larger with the magnifier, or take it off with “Remove from dashboard”: the chart stays saved in its dataset. On the dashboard, charts use all the rows, with no filters.
guidaPagina.p7Testo: In “My account” you can download all your data or delete the account along with everything you uploaded. Your files are visible only to you.
guidaPagina.nota: The app shows your data and does not give medical advice.
